The basic argument for complete antinatalism is that humanity is effectively a cancer that will destroy the entire ecosystem if left unchecked, and even a few survivors will continue the cycle. Even though I can see some reasoning that supports the idea of humanity being likened to a cancer of this ecosystem, I cannot support the idea that humanity's extinction is necessary to being the ecosystem into remission.

However, I can support a lot of arguments for partial or personal antinatalism. A given person who does not want to have children should not be required or expected to have them. We are at the point where we are using resources at a faster rate than they are replenished, so the population must decrease, probably by at least half, if we want to be a sustainable species. If we could go for 40 years without any human reproducing, we'd be just fine.

I also am struggling to find a legitimate, non-selfish argument for pronatalism. Ask anyone why they had kids, and their first two words will be "I wanted" or "We wanted."

I personally am probably in this camp. I don't understand why people feel this need to populate the earth (probably biological and not logical) when it is already under such a heavy burden. There's a lot of things we need. We don't need more people.
